title: Demurrage and Detention Free Time: which clock the final detention line is measured on
content:
## Scope

For the final detention line of a per-container record under the AHL Demurrage and Detention Free Time category, this rule fixes the clock whose days are measured, its start and stop dates, the days it has used and the free days it is measured against. It depends on the clock model of the product on the record and on whether the record is an import or an export record.

## Rule

1. **Separate clock model.** The detention clock of an import record runs from the full gate-out date to the empty return date against the import detention free days; that of an export record runs from the empty pickup date to the full gate-in date against the export detention free days.
2. **Combined clock model.** The merged clock of an import record runs from the discharge date to the empty return date, and that of an export record from the empty pickup date to the loading date, against the merged free days of the direction.
3. The days used are the stop date minus the start date in calendar days. Stated in the product's own day count, they are the calendar days from the start date to the stop date, less the product's clock start offset, increased by one; with an offset of one day both readings give the same figure.

## Clock selection table

| Clock model | Record | Start date | Stop date | Free days measured against |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| separate | import | full gate-out | empty return | import detention free days |
| separate | export | empty pickup | full gate-in | export detention free days |
| combined | import | discharge | empty return | merged import free days |
| combined | export | empty pickup | loading | merged export free days |

## Worked example (hypothetical dates, offset of one day)

- Separate model, import record: full gate-out on 3 April, empty return on 12 April. The detention clock has used 9 days, 12 April less 3 April.
- Combined model, export record: empty pickup on 1 July, loading on 26 July. The merged clock has used 25 days, and the gate-in date does not shorten this clock.

## Wrong reading and correct basis

| Wrong reading | Correct basis |
|---|---|
| "On a combined record the detention clock starts at full gate-out." | Under the combined model the merged clock starts at discharge on import and at empty pickup on export. |
| "An export detention clock under the separate model ends at loading." | Under the separate model it ends at full gate-in. |
